envelope.text: with the one option it has

why:
phase-427 W9 (2026-09-07) — LANDED. `struct InitOptions { domain_id: Option<u32> }` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:182`) with `new()`, `Default`, `with_domain_id(self, Option<usize>) -> Self` (`:199`, rclrs's signature — `usize` there; a value above `u32::MAX` saturates and the consuming constructor refuses it as `DomainIdOutOfRange`, since a builder has no `Result` to carry the refusal) its in-place twin `set_domain_id(&mut self, Option<usize>)` (`:204`, which the first parity run reported as the one theirs-only member of a type that now correlates `same`) and a `domain_id()` accessor. Compiles on EVERY target — it holds no string. Consumed by `Context::from_env` and `Context::new`.

ADOPT-BOUNDED: rclrs's `InitOptions` has exactly this one field today, so the adoption is complete against the current upstream; the bound is that this is the ONLY option there will be here — a hosted-only option rclrs might add (anything that names the rcl allocator or the argv parse) is absent, and `with_domain_id` is the one setter upstream tutorials use. The platform constraint is the one on the constructors that consume it: freestanding, the override lands on the BAKED context. Test: `init_options_default_overrides_nothing` (`--features alloc`).

History: `divergence` / `theirs-only` ("the domain arrives through the boot-config ladder, not a mutable options object"), decided 2026-09-07 (RFC-0089 "Context and `init`, settled") and landed.

phase-467 — `domain_id()` returns `Option<usize>` now, which is rclrs's type and the type `with_domain_id` / `set_domain_id` already took. It returned `Option<u32>`, the STORED width, so the two setters spoke rclrs and the getter spoke the field; the closed `rust:Context::domain_id` row cited all three as already speaking `usize` and was two thirds right, which is why the inconsistency it argued FROM had to be fixed in the same pass rather than displaced onto `Context`. The saturation is unchanged and lives in the stored `u32`: a round trip through `u32::MAX + 1` still reports `u32::MAX`, and the refusal still lands on the consuming constructor as `DomainIdOutOfRange`, which is the one place with a `Result` to carry it. Four in-crate assertions moved; there is no other caller.
